basic_information.official_title: AN ACT EXTENDING THE VALIDITY OF THE GENERAL APPROPRIATIONS ACT OF THE BANGSAMORO FOR FISCAL YEAR 2023 UNTIL DECEMBER 31, 2024, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE SECTION 50 OF BANGSAMORO AUTONOMY ACT NO. 32, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
signed_by: Prof. Raby B. Angkal, Secretary General
basic_information.effectivity: Immediately after publication in a newspaper of regional circulation

citizen_summary.what_is_this_about: Extends the 2023 Bangsamoro budget to the end of 2024 — and closes a loophole by ruling that money merely transferred between offices or to a local government does not count as spent until it actually pays for something delivered.
citizen_summary.why_was_it_proposed: The 2023 appropriations were about to lapse with works unfinished. Parliament used the same act to tighten what counts as disbursement and to protect local government units' tax shares.
citizen_summary.what_will_change: Most 2023 appropriations stayed releasable and obligable to 31 December 2024, with obligated infrastructure and operating items valid until fully expended. Unreleased money lapses and unspent money reverts to the Treasury. Transfers between units no longer count as disbursement.
who_will_be_affected: Constituent local government units, whose national tax shares are protected until fully released, obligated and disbursed
Anyone concerned with whether budgeted money is actually spent on what it was voted for
citizen_summary.when_will_it_take_effect: Took effect immediately on publication at the end of 2023.

what_this_means_for_you.in_short: NOW LAW. The 2023 budget ran to end-2024 — and money shuffled between offices or handed to an LGU is not treated as spent until it actually pays for completed work.
in_practice: 2023 appropriations available for release and obligation until 31 December 2024
Amounts obligated by that date for infrastructure completion, and for MOOE under Support to Operations and Operations and other capital outlays, stay valid until fully expended
Unreleased appropriations lapse; unexpended funds revert to the Bangsamoro Treasury under a Special Fund for reappropriation
Constituent LGUs' shares in national taxes collected in the BARMM remain available until fully released, obligated and disbursed

Funds transferred between organisational units, between ministries, or to LGUs are not considered disbursed until actually used to pay for completed construction, goods delivered and services rendered, inspected and accepted within the validity period
Personnel Services and MOOE under General Administration and Support were obligable only to 31 December 2023
The Special Development Fund's validity is left to a separate law

for_specific_groups.Local government units: Your share of national taxes collected in the region is protected — it remains available until fully released, obligated and disbursed, notwithstanding anything else in the section.
for_specific_groups.Anyone auditing spending: Section 1's transfer rule is the important one: a ministry cannot beat a deadline by moving money to another unit or to an LGU and calling it disbursed.
for_specific_groups.Contractors: Obligated infrastructure and operating items remain valid until fully expended.

what_this_means_for_you.where_this_applies: The Bangsamoro Government's fiscal year 2023 appropriations.
what_this_means_for_you.when_you_will_feel_it: In force since the end of 2023.
what_you_can_do: Ask whether money reported as disbursed actually paid for work completed, inspected and accepted — that is now the statutory test
Ask your LGU about its share of national taxes collected in the region, which this act protects
watch_out_for: Obligated amounts remain valid 'until fully expended', so there is no final payment date once money is committed.
The Special Development Fund is carved out and governed by its own law — see BAA 51.
Personnel Services and General Administration and Support MOOE were not extended beyond 2023.

key_terms_explained.Release: Making an appropriation available to a spending agency.
key_terms_explained.Obligation: Committing money to a contract or purchase.
key_terms_explained.Disbursement: Actually paying money out — which this act redefines to exclude mere transfers.
key_terms_explained.Reversion: Unspent money returning to the Treasury, here into a Special Fund for reappropriation under the Organic Law.
key_terms_explained.GAS: General Administration and Support — the overhead category excluded from the extension.

what_this_means_for_you.status_note: Passed Jumada Al-Akhirah 07, 1445 / 20 December 2023, approved by the Chief Minister on 29 December 2023.

benefits.headline: A year's extension for the 2023 budget, plus a statutory test for what counts as actually spending money.

direct_benefits.benefit: 2023-funded projects and operations could continue through 2024
Protection of LGU shares in national taxes until fully released, obligated and disbursed
direct_benefits.how_to_access: Stated notwithstanding any other provision or issuance

direct_benefits.benefit: A rule that transferred funds are not 'disbursed' until they pay for delivered work
direct_benefits.who_gets_it: Anyone relying on spending reports being meaningful

indirect_benefits: Clear reversion of unspent funds to the Treasury for reappropriation
limitations: Obligated amounts have no final payment date.
The Special Development Fund is excluded and governed separately.

for_citizens: None. The act governs government spending.

what_is_prohibited: The act defines no prohibited acts for the public. Its restriction falls on agencies: treating a transfer of funds as a disbursement before the money has actually paid for completed and accepted work.

penalties.for_citizens: None. The act creates no offence, fine or imprisonment.
penalties.note: Ministries, offices and agencies are directed to strictly observe the validity of appropriations and the reversion of funds; no sanction is stated in this act.

where_to_complain.first_stop: Ministry of Finance, and Budget and Management (MFBM), authorised to issue the implementing guidelines
where_to_complain.note: The act creates no complaints procedure of its own.

everyday_scenarios: A ministry transfers project money to a municipality in December to avoid the deadline. Under Section 1 that is not a disbursement — the money only counts as spent once it has paid for completed construction or goods delivered, inspected and accepted.
An LGU worries its share of national taxes will lapse. The act says those shares remain available until fully released, obligated and disbursed, notwithstanding the rest of the section.

key_provisions: Section 1 — Amends Section 50 of Bangsamoro Autonomy Act No. 32 (the FY2023 General Appropriations Act). All appropriations are available for release and obligation until 31 December 2024. Amounts obligated as of that date for the completion of construction, inspection and payment of Infrastructure Capital Outlays, and for delivery, inspection and payment of MOOE under Support to Operations and Operations and other capital outlays, remain valid until fully expended. After the validity period, unreleased appropriations lapse and unexpended or undisbursed funds revert to the Bangsamoro Treasury under a Special Fund for reappropriation under Section 19, Article XII of RA 11054. Notwithstanding that provision and any other issuance, the shares of constituent LGUs in national taxes collected in the BARMM remain available until fully released, obligated and disbursed. Funds transferred between organisational units within a ministry, office or agency, between ministries, offices or agencies, or by them to LGUs, are not considered disbursed until the transferred amounts have actually been used to pay for completed construction, goods delivered and services rendered, inspected and accepted within the validity period, with transfers strictly in accordance with budgeting, accounting, auditing and procurement laws.

Section 2 — Inserts Section 50-A into BAA 32: Personnel Services and MOOE under General Administration and Support are valid for obligation only until 31 December 2023, and the extension of the Special Development Fund's validity is governed by a law enacted for the purpose.
Section 4 — Takes effect immediately after publication in a newspaper of regional circulation.

impact.allocated_budget: No new appropriation. It extends the FY2023 budget enacted by BAA 32.
impact.figures_note: The act states no amount — it changes deadlines and the definition of disbursement.

citizen_questions.q: What is the most useful thing in this act?
citizen_questions.a: The rule that money transferred between government units, or handed to a local government, is not counted as disbursed until it has actually paid for completed construction, goods delivered or services rendered, inspected and accepted.
Release and obligation to 31 December 2024. Once obligated, infrastructure and certain operating items remain valid until fully expended.

citizen_questions.q: What happens to money never spent?
citizen_questions.a: Unreleased appropriations lapse, and unexpended or undisbursed funds revert to the Bangsamoro Treasury under a Special Fund for reappropriation.

citizen_questions.q: Are local government tax shares affected?
citizen_questions.a: They are protected. Notwithstanding the rest of the section, constituent LGUs' shares in national taxes collected in the region remain available until fully released, obligated and disbursed.

citizen_questions.q: Does this cover the Special Development Fund?
citizen_questions.a: No. Section 50-A expressly leaves that to a separate law — BAA 51, passed the same day.
